subject: Inference deployment options — private/VPC vs hyperscalers evaluation
messages:
From: Connor O'BRIEN <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@fintechco.com>, Aaron Castillo <a.castillo@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Recap + next tests: Private/VPC vs hyperscalers (post-call)

Samantha / Aaron — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary driver: predictable inference cost and strict controls over data residency and key management for transaction-level models.
- Comparing two paths: (A) hyperscaler-managed endpoints (Bedrock/Vertex) for speed of onboarding vs (B) Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for control, auditability, and air-gapped options.
- Need: a short, focused set of tests to compare p99 latency, throughput per GPU, and an estimate of unit cost (tokens/sec + infra amortized) across the candidates.

What Redwood will provide
- A short matrix comparing capability/controls (attached): redwood-vs-hyperscalers-matrix.xlsx
- A network checklist + suggested port/IP ranges for a VPC-peered Private deployment (we'll follow up with a PDF).
- A proposed PoC test plan: 1) latency/throughput baseline (synthetic load), 2) cold-start behavior, 3) KV-cache hit-rate impact for typical session sizes.

Questions for you
- Is the control plane required to live in your VPC (customer-managed) or is an outbound-only control plane acceptable?
- Is air-gapped/on-prem required for the PoC or just for final production?
- Can you share the contact for your infra/networking lead so we can align the checklist?

Proposed next steps
1) You confirm desired control-plane model and whether air-gap is required for the PoC.
2) We run the small three-test suite (we can run endpoints in our hosted env + your VPC Private instance) — target window next week.
3) Follow up with a short readout + cost comparison.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks — I copied Marissa and Vivek so we have SE support on the technical details. If that sounds good I'll send the network checklist and a calendar invite for kickoff.

—
Connor O'BRIEN
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0148
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: Recap + next tests: Private/VPC vs hyperscalers (post-call)

Connor — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying items before we lock the PoC window:

1) Control plane: for production we need the control plane in our account/VPC (customer-managed). For the PoC we are flexible — outbound-only is OK if we can validate key controls (no raw logs leaving our VPC).
2) KMS/HSM: we require Customer-Managed KMS for model keys and HSM-backed signing for audit-critical ops.
3) Network: we will need a one-way ingress arrangement and clear port/IP lists.
4) Pricing: Can you provide a ballpark monthly and per-token estimate for Reserved capacity (we'll share expected QPS).

Please send the network checklist and the PoC test plan. I'm looping in our infra lead Aaron and procurement so we can coordinate access and contract questions.

Thanks —
Samantha Li
Head of ML Platforms | FinTechCo
samantha.li@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@fintechco.com>
Cc: Connor O'BRIEN <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-16T11:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next tests: Private/VPC vs hyperscalers (post-call)

Hi Samantha — appreciate the details. I'm Marissa (SE) and I'll take point on the technical PoC. Answering your questions and adding specifics below. (Quoted for context)

> Control plane requirement: production must be in customer VPC

That maps cleanly to our Redwood Private offering. Two viable deployment patterns for the PoC:
- Customer-managed control plane (recommended): control plane components run in your VPC via PrivateLink/peering; data plane in dedicated Redwood nodes (can be hosted in your project/region). Control plane APIs are internal-only.
- Outbound-only control plane (fastest for PoC): our control plane accepts egress-only connections and the model execution happens in a dedicated VPC; we ensure no retention of raw request bodies unless explicitly enabled.

KMS/HSM
- We support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HashiCorp Vault HSM integrations. For strict compliance we can offer HSM-backed key operations (FIPS 140-2) and bring-your-own-key ownership model.

Network requirements (high level)
- Ports: 443 outbound for control-plane telemetry (if outbound-only).
- For customer-managed control plane: we publish a CIDR list and port matrix (attached: networking-checklist.pdf). We can also do an iptables profile for an air-gapped node.

Air-gapped/on-prem
- We offer an air-gapped on-prem package for high-reg compliance: no external control-plane endpoints, local-only control plane. Installation requires a staging VM that our engineers coordinate with your infra team. This usually adds 2–4 weeks for validation, depending on procurement cadence.

Suggested PoC test matrix (we'll run these both against Bedrock/Vertex and Redwood Private so you get apples-to-apples):
1) Synthetic latency/throughput: 1k/2k token sequences, measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
2) Cold-start: measure first-request latency after instance spin-up.
3) KV-cache effectiveness: evaluate hit-rate impact on multi-turn sessions.
4) Cost estimate: estimate per-1M token cost given observed throughput + infra assumptions.

Attachments: networking-checklist.pdf (pdf), private-deploy-arch.png (png)

Logistics
- To run the customer-managed control plane PoC we'll need temporary network access from your infra team and an installer-run window (~2 hours).
- Can Aaron share available windows next Wednesday or Thursday?

I'll prepare the installer artifact and a short runbook for the infra team once we confirm the window. Happy to jump on a quick technical call with Aaron and your SREs.

—
Marissa Cole
